testcase.name: (a) enqueue commits with the business change and rolls back with it
(b) app_worker dequeues under FORCE; the table owner and app_api cannot read
(c) max attempts are carried on the job
(d) dead jobs are visible (attempts >= max_attempts)
app_api is refused DELETE and the views (BR-F04-2 evidence of the actual grants)
(c) back-off: a failing job is rescheduled later with attempts incremented
publish fans out one job per registered handler in the caller transaction
install is repeatable after the ownership handover and keeps the hardening
A-1 app_api: direct SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on every queue table, view and sequence are refused
A-1 app_api: library functions are refused (add_job, get_job, reschedule_jobs, permanently_fail_jobs, force_unlock_workers)
A-1 refused identifiers: unknown, system, data_repair, malformed; nothing is stored
A-1 the task_type CHECK refuses api_enqueue for system and data_repair
A-1 each argument bound is refused at limit + 1 and accepted at the limit
A-1 max_attempts comes from task_type; a job key from task A cannot replace task B's job
A-1 replace mode: same task and key replaces the unstarted job
A-1 hostile search_path and temp-schema shadowing have no effect
A-1 enqueue commits and rolls back with the caller transaction
A-1 a type missing from task_type fails closed and rolls the caller back
A-1 app_worker: direct add_job in the same namespace and the dequeue cycle still work
A-1 install revoked every app_api right in queue and a repeat install keeps it
RLS under withScope: an organisation sees only its rows; a handle without scope sees none
settings do not leak past the transaction (transaction-local)
concurrent duplicate keys give one write and one replay; a different body gives a conflict
